name: Elishama
overview: Elishama was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified uniquely as the son of Jekamiah according to 1 Chronicles 2:41. Beyond this familial connection, Scripture provides limited additional details about his life or role. His mention situates him within the genealogical records important for understanding the lineage of Judah.
namesAndTitles: The name Elishama means 'G-d [El] has heard,' reflecting a theologically rich Hebrew name that acknowledges God's attentive nature. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries significant meaning rooted in divine responsiveness, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 2:41.
familyAndRelationships: Elishama is recorded specifically as the son of Jekamiah. Scripture does not provide further family relationships beyond this connection, limiting our understanding of his broader familial context.
scriptureSignificance: Elishama's significance lies primarily in his place within the genealogical framework of Judah, which is crucial for tracing the lineage through which God's promises and covenantal blessings were fulfilled. His mention in 1 Chronicles 2:41 contributes to the biblical record that establishes the heritage of the people of God, underscoring the faithfulness of God in preserving His chosen line.
